questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Seoul because I wanted to study at a university that was as different as possible from my home university. I was especially interested in experiencing a new culture, meeting new people, and being surrounded by a different language. I also saw the exchange as an opportunity to explore Korean culture and have new experiences outside of my studies.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a little difficult to find and navigate all the necessary information upon arrival. The university’s website could be somewhat confusing, especially when it came to finding important dates and deadlines.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We received a very warm welcome when we arrived. The university organised an introduction day on campus, where they told us about the university’s history and provided useful practical information. They also made an effort to help us get settled and create a social community among the exchange students, which made the arrival and adjustment much easier.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I was assigned a room in C-House, one of the university’s on-campus dormitories for exchange students.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was a large shared kitchen available in the dormitory. There was no meal plan, so we were responsible for buying our own groceries and preparing our own meals.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Living on campus was a great way to meet other exchange students and be part of a social community. The staff were also very kind, helpful, and welcoming, which made living there a pleasant experience.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was somewhat difficult to navigate. It was not always easy to find and understand the available courses, and the university’s website could be confusing. Some of the emails and information provided were also difficult to understand.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: However, the staff were very helpful and responsive whenever I had questions or needed clarification.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Ended up being very succesful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would recommend starting the registration process well in advance. Take your time to understand the available courses and the different steps involved, as the information can be somewhat difficult to navigate. Preparing early will make the process much easier and less stressful.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took a combination of both Bachelor’s and Master’s level courses, as this was the most appropriate option for my academic background and study programme.  The courses provided a good balance and allowed me to choose subjects that were relevant to my education.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style at my host institution was somewhat different from UCPH. The classes were generally more structured, with a stronger focus on attendance, participation, and continuous work throughout the semester. I also experienced a more formal classroom environment compared to UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Health and Urban Life: very interesting course with a different perspective that I found highly relevant to my studies in health and society.
Environment and History in East Asia: An engaging course that provided an interesting perspective on the historical and environmental development of East Asia.
Mental Health Problems: A very interesting course with good and engaging teachers. It offered useful perspectives that were relevant to my academic background.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a wide variety of cultural, athletic, and social activities available for students. There were different sports and fitness activities, as well as music and other cultural events. There were also plenty of opportunities to meet other students and take part in social activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: participating in a sport at skku - social engagement

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend making the most of your weekends and holidays by exploring South Korea outside of Seoul. Going on hikes is a great way to experience the beautiful nature, while visiting museums offers an opportunity to learn more about Korean history and culture. I would also recommend visiting other cities around South Korea, as each place offers a different experience. e.g Busan, Sokcho, Jeongju, Jeju Island

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy to adjust to the local culture. Although some aspects were different from what I was used to, people were very kind, welcoming, and open, which made the transition easier. The main challenge was the language barrier, as not everyone spoke English.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I would recommend joining running clubs or other sports activities, as these are great ways to meet local students and make connections. It is also worth attending university events, concerts, and other social activities where local and exchange students can interact.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The main challenge was the language barrier, as not everyone spoke English.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Kindness, extremely polite people

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Prepare well in advance - The registration process and information on courses can be confusing, so make sure to read everything carefully and start preparing early.
Get involved socially - Join sports clubs, events, concerts, or other activities to meet both local and international students and make the most of your exchange.
Explore beyond Seoul - Take the opportunity to travel around South Korea, go hiking, visit museums, and experience different cities and parts of the country.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was meeting so many new people and building friendships with people from different countries and backgrounds. The friendships I made and the experiences we shared were definitely one of the highlights of my exchange.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was probably adjusting to the language barrier and navigating some of the practical information from the university. However, these challenges also encouraged me to become more independent and adaptable.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
